full_text_en:
Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C v. Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau — application for appointment of estate administrator

【Ruling Summary】

After the commencement of inheritance, if there is no heir, a person who has no statutory duty to support the decedent but has in fact provided considerable support meets the condition under Article 1131 of the Civil Code of the PRC that "an appropriate share of the estate may be given", and has a legal interest in the proper preservation of the estate, and is entitled to apply to the people's court for appointment of an estate administrator.

Applicant: Gu A, male, born on October 22, 1954, Han Chinese, residing in Taicang City, Jiangsu Province.

Applicant: Gu B, male, born on February 24, 1946, Han Chinese, residing in Taicang City, Jiangsu Province.

Applicant: Gu C, male, born on July 12, 1961, Han Chinese, residing in Taicang City, Jiangsu Province.

Respondent: Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau, domiciled at Xianfu Street, Taicang City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yuezhong, Director of the Bureau.

The applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C filed a lawsuit with the Taicang People's Court, Jiangsu Province, against the respondent Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau regarding the application for appointment of an estate administrator.

The applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C alleged: Yang Biwu and Yang Qiben were siblings. The house located at Room XX, Building X, Shixiao Lane, Chengxiang Town, Taicang City, was registered under Yang Biwu's name. After Yang Biwu's death, her only heir was Yang Qiben, and the estate including the said house should belong to Yang Qiben. Yang Biwu and Yang Qiben were elderly persons living alone, and the three applicants had been caring for them during their lifetimes. Yang Biwu was hospitalized for the last eight years of her life, and the daily care was also borne by the three applicants; Yang Qiben was unable to care for himself, and the three applicants basically took care of him on a daily basis and also helped hire a nursing assistant for him. Yang Qiben was admitted to LuDu Xin'an Rehabilitation Hospital for medical and nursing care on October 15, 2017. The three applicants visited Yang Qiben every other day, and later, due to epidemic prevention and control requirements, visited once a week until Yang Qiben died in the hospital on January 30, 2021. The funeral arrangements for both Yang Biwu and Yang Qiben were handled by the three applicants, and on each ancestor worship day, the three applicants conducted rituals according to local customs. Since Yang Qiben left no heir after his death, and the three applicants have an interest in this property, pursuant to Article 1145 of the Civil Code of the PRC, they applied to the court to designate the respondent Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau as the estate administrator of Yang Qiben.

The respondent Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau argued: It had no objection to the facts alleged by the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C, but was not aware of the living conditions and the status of the estate of Yang Biwu and Yang Qiben during their lifetimes, and that the two elderly persons were more often cared for by the residents' committee of their place of residence. Therefore, it would be more appropriate for the Fudong Community Residents Committee of Chengxiang Town, Taicang City, to serve as the estate administrator. Whether the three applicants qualify as interested persons should be determined by the court.

The court of first instance, Taicang People's Court, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts:

Yang Biwu (born on August 18, 1929) and Yang Qiben (born on December 23, 1930) were siblings. Their parents predeceased them, and both were unmarried, without spouses, and had no other siblings. Yang Biwu died on June 8, 2014, and Yang Qiben died on January 30, 2021. During their lifetimes, they lived in the house located at Room XX, Building X, Shixiao Lane, Chengxiang Town, Taicang City, for which the land use right and house ownership were registered under Yang Biwu's name.

Gu Fengdi and Gu Jingbo were the grandparents of the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C. Gu Fengdi was Yang Qiben's wet nurse.

It was also found that: Yang Qiben was a deaf-mute person with disabilities. After Yang Biwu's death, when the relevant government authorities coordinated arrangements for Yang Qiben's living, Yang Qiben chose to have the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C take care of him in his old age.

Because Yang Qiben was unable to care for himself, the applicants Gu A and Gu B provided daily care for him and helped hire a nursing assistant. On September 24, 2017, Yang Qiben was treated at Taicang Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine for illness and was diagnosed with "cerebral infarction, hypertension, and pneumonia." After treatment at Taicang Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, he was transferred to Taicang Xin'an Rehabilitation Hospital on October 15, 2017, for inpatient treatment until his death on January 30, 2021. During his stay at Taicang Xin'an Rehabilitation Hospital, the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C visited him regularly, and the nursing costs, meal expenses, and medical expenses during hospitalization were all handled by Gu A. After Yang Qiben's death, the three applicants handled his funeral arrangements. Subsequently, Gu A applied to his community and had the cremated remains of Yang Biwu, Yang Qiben, and their parents placed together in the collective shrine of Xianghuaqiao Community, Loudong Street, Taicang City. On each ancestor worship day, the three applicants conducted rituals according to local customs.

During the trial, upon investigation with the Fudong Community Residents Committee of Chengxiang Town, Taicang City, where Yang Biwu and Yang Qiben lived before their deaths, the residents' committee confirmed the facts stated by the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C, and stated that the three applicants were the persons designated by Yang Qiben and Yang Biwu to take care of them, and that the three applicants had fulfilled their care obligations towards the two elderly persons.

The court of first instance, Taicang People's Court, Jiangsu Province, held:

Article 1145 of the Civil Code of the PRC provides: "After the commencement of inheritance, if there is an executor of the will, the executor shall be the estate administrator; if there is no executor of the will, the heirs shall promptly elect an estate administrator; if the heirs fail to elect, the heirs shall jointly serve as the estate administrator; if there is no heir or all heirs renounce the inheritance, the civil affairs department or the villagers' committee of the decedent's place of domicile before death shall serve as the estate administrator." Article 1146 provides: "If there is a dispute over the determination of the estate administrator, an interested person may apply to the people's court for appointment of an estate administrator."

In this case, after Yang Biwu's death, she had no first-order heir, and Yang Qiben, as a second-order heir, was entitled to inherit the estate including the property in question. Pursuant to Article 230 of the Civil Code of the PRC, the acquisition of real rights through inheritance takes effect from the commencement of the inheritance. Therefore, Yang Qiben had acquired the real rights to the corresponding estate, including the property in question, registered under Yang Biwu's name through inheritance. Now that Yang Qiben died on January 30, 2021, leaving no heir, this situation falls within the circumstances for applying for appointment of an estate administrator as defined in Articles 1145 and 1146 of the Civil Code of the PRC.

Because the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C provided considerable support to Yang Qiben during his lifetime, they meet the condition under Article 1131 of the Civil Code of the PRC that "an appropriate share of the estate may be given," and thus the three applicants have the right, as interested persons, to apply to the people's court for appointment of an estate administrator.

First, in accordance with Article 1131 of the Civil Code of the PRC, a person other than an heir who has provided considerable support to the decedent may be given an appropriate share of the estate. This article, based on the principle of consistency of rights and obligations, grants a person other than an heir who has provided considerable support to the decedent the right to receive a discretionary share of the estate. In this case, the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C are not heirs of Yang Qiben, but they took great care of Yang Qiben's daily needs, such as diet and medical care, and provided considerable assistance in his life. Since the three applicants provided de facto support to Yang Qiben and fulfilled substantial support obligations, under the above legal provision, they meet the condition under Article 1131 of the Civil Code of the PRC that "an appropriate share of the estate may be given," and are entitled to apply for appointment of an estate administrator as interested persons.

Second, in this case, although the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C are not related to Yang Qiben by blood or marriage and have no statutory duty to support Yang Qiben, due to the specific relationship between their grandparents and Yang Qiben, the three applicants had close ties with Yang Qiben in life. Most importantly, Yang Qiben chose the three applicants to care for him in his old age, and the three applicants diligently cared for and accompanied Yang Qiben for many years, providing him with emotional comfort until his death from illness, allowing him to enjoy his later years. After Yang Qiben's death, the three applicants handled all his funeral arrangements and conducted ancestor worship according to customs, which is consistent with the traditional virtues of the Chinese nation in supporting the elderly and helping the disabled, and is a concrete manifestation of good socialist morals and customs, which should be encouraged. Therefore, allowing the three applicants to apply for appointment of an estate administrator as interested persons is conducive to promoting the socialist core values of civility, harmony, integrity, and friendship.

Third, in the absence of a determined estate administrator, there is a risk of damage, loss, or misappropriation of the estate, which may harm the rights and interests of interested persons such as heirs, legatees, and estate creditors. To prevent such harm, the Civil Code establishes the estate administrator system to ensure the safety of the estate and the legitimate interests of relevant civil subjects. In this case, Yang Qiben has no statutory heirs, legatees, or estate creditors. If the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C are not allowed to apply for appointment of an estate administrator, it would be detrimental to the preservation, management, and disposal of the estate.

Given that the civil affairs department undertakes duties such as social relief, social welfare undertakings, and community services, is relatively familiar with the family relationships and property status of citizens within its jurisdiction, and has the capacity to serve as an estate administrator, the request of the applicants Gu A, Gu B, and Gu C to designate the civil affairs department of Yang Qiben's place of domicile before death, namely Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau, as the estate administrator is supported in accordance with the law.

Pursuant to Article 1147 of the Civil Code of the PRC, the duties of Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau as the estate administrator of Yang Qiben are: (1) to inventory the estate and prepare a list of the estate; (2) to report the status of the estate to the heirs; (3) to take necessary measures to prevent damage or loss of the estate; (4) to handle the decedent's claims and debts; (5) to distribute the estate in accordance with the will or pursuant to legal provisions; and (6) to perform other necessary acts related to the administration of the estate.

In conclusion, the Taicang People's Court, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Articles 1127, 1131, 1145, 1146, and 1147 of the Civil Code of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on December 7, 2022:

Taicang Civil Affairs Bureau is designated as the estate administrator of Yang Qiben.
